destination.name: Kosciuszko National Park
destination.tagline: Mainland Australia's highest peaks, with snow resorts in winter and alpine walks in summer.
destination.description: Kosciuszko National Park covers about 6,900 square kilometres in the south-east of New South Wales and contains Mount Kosciuszko, the highest peak on the Australian mainland. The mountains are typically under metres-deep snow for up to four months of the year, and Thredbo, Perisher and Charlotte Pass ski resorts lie within the park. In summer many thousands walk to the summit, 6 km from the Thredbo chairlift or 9 km from Charlotte Pass. Charlotte Pass recorded Australia's lowest temperature, -23 degrees Celsius, in June 1994.
whyVisit: Ride Thredbo's chairlift into the alpine

goodToKnow.title: Snow chains in winter
goodToKnow.detail: 2WD vehicles must carry chains on the Alpine Way, Kosciuszko Road and Guthega Road in winter, and some rental companies forbid taking cars past Jindabyne.

goodToKnow.title: Summit walk is seasonal
goodToKnow.detail: The track to the top is snowbound from June to October, and Charlotte Pass has no car access in those months; summer chairlifts at Thredbo run November to April.

goodToKnow.title: Park entry fee
goodToKnow.detail: A park entry fee applies, about $17 to $29 a day depending on season; check NPWS before you go.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are the walking months, when the summit tracks are clear of snow; the ski season runs through winter instead.
